plugins.name: ship
plugins.description: A gated idea-to-production pipeline for Claude Code: research -> spec -> build -> layered QA (functional + eval + a parallel expert-agent panel) -> prod-prep -> provision -> deploy -> monitor, with reusable doc templates (including a gitleaks pre-commit + CI secret scan). Owner sign-off gates and per-phase state keep routine delivery steps from being skipped. Beta.

skills.name: ship-build
skills.description: Phase 3 (and Fix, phase 5) of the ship pipeline — implement the frozen spec to the code map, wire the local→staging→prod environments and secrets, and keep progress.md current. Use when the spec is frozen and it's time to write code, or to close QA findings during the fix phase.
headings: Gate — Build → phase 4 · Fix → re-run QA (phase 4), then phase 6 when clean

skills.name: ship-deploy
skills.description: Phase 8 of the ship pipeline — deploy to production and smoke-test. Push code, run migrations, restart services, verify /health + robots/sitemap + redirects, and purge CDN cache. Use when the host is provisioned and a build is ready to go live, or to run a routine deploy.
headings: Deploy loop (build once, promote one artifact)

skills.name: ship-expert-qa
skills.description: Phase 4 of the ship pipeline — layered QA. Run functional tests + eval/calibration, then fan out a parallel panel of expert reviewers (SEO, code, UI/UX, security, devops), each writing an audit file, then triage findings into critical/major/minor. Use when a build is ready for review, when the user says "QA this", "review before launch", or "run the expert panel".
headings: Layer A — functional + CI (RUN; failures become findings, not gate-blocks)
Layer A.5 — browser journey (MANDATORY for any project with a UI)
Layer B — eval / calibration (for scored or model-driven logic)
Layer C — expert agent panel (fan-out, parallel)
Layer C.5 — verification (before any human sees findings)
Triage (you do this on the VERIFIED findings)
Gate — exit QA (complete, not necessarily clean)

skills.name: ship-monitor
skills.description: Phase 9 of the ship pipeline — monitor in production and feed iteration. Confirm uptime/alerting works, set up a standing monitoring cadence, watch errors/metrics, and turn findings into the next ROADMAP items. Use after launch, or when the user wants ongoing monitoring, a post-launch check, or to plan the next iteration.

skills.name: ship-prod-prep
skills.description: Phase 6 of the ship pipeline — prepare production. Fill the production runbook, TLS/reverse proxy, DNS + domain canonicalization + redirects, Cloudflare/WAF, secrets with locked perms, backups/snapshots on a schedule, uptime + alerting, and email deliverability (SPF/DKIM/DMARC). Use when QA passes and the project is heading to launch.
headings: CI / paved road (generate working config, not docs)
Email deliverability (if the app sends mail)

skills.name: ship-provision
skills.description: Phase 7 of the ship pipeline — stand up the server and access. Provision the VM, create and lock down SSH keys, install systemd services + timers, configure the firewall, and record it all in the runbook. Use when it's time to create/configure the production host, set up SSH, or wire systemd/backups on the server.

skills.name: ship-research
skills.description: Phase 1 of the ship pipeline — research a project idea WITHOUT implementing. Gather market/competitor/keyword/audience/buyer-language evidence, synthesize a capstone analysis and a repo-grounded execution plan, and end with open questions for the owner. Use when the user says "research this", "before we build", or the ship orchestrator enters phase 1.

skills.name: ship-seo-strategy
skills.description: Plan how a project gets found and adopted — SEO/go-to-market research and a promotion plan. Use when the user asks how to promote/market/rank a project, wants keyword or competitor research, a content/distribution plan, or during the ship research phase for anything with a marketing surface. Not an on-page audit (that's ship-seo-expert / the QA phase) — this is growth strategy.

skills.name: ship-spec
skills.description: Phase 2 of the ship pipeline — turn approved research into a frozen spec. Extend the phase-0 CONSTITUTION.md (non-negotiable principles, the single source) with project-specific rules, and write PROJECT.md (full reference), CLAUDE.md (the Claude Code guide — project-specific rules + code map), ACCEPTANCE.md (machine-checkable criteria), ROADMAP.md, and the env matrix. Use when research is approved and it's time to define data model, routes, and non-negotiable rules before building.

skills.name: ship
skills.description: Drive a project from idea to production through a gated pipeline — research → spec → build → layered QA (functional + eval + a parallel expert-agent panel) → prod-prep → provision → deploy → monitor. Use when starting a new project, resuming one, or when the user says "take this to production", "ship it", "what's the next step", or asks to plan a project end-to-end. Enforces phase gates and owner sign-off to reduce skipped steps and keep delivery evidence visible.
headings: Transitions (how phases advance — not a strict +1 march)
Guardrails carried into every project (from the real repos)

commands.name: expert-review
commands.description: Run the parallel expert-QA panel (SEO, code, UI/UX, security, devops) on the current project and triage the findings.

commands.name: gate
commands.description: Check whether a ship pipeline phase's gate is met and compute the next phase — executable validation (checks/QA/judge/quality/owner) + transition, then record evidence to .ship/state.yml.

commands.name: go
commands.description: Compatibility alias for Claude Code's namespaced command surface. The primary Desktop/Cowork entry is the ship skill.

commands.name: handoff
commands.description: Generate a _HANDOFF.md that packages draft artifacts for another agent/session — with hard rules baked in and explicit owner sign-off items.

commands.name: new-project
commands.description: Scaffold a new project at phase 0 — the placeholder-free working set (positioning, constitution, progress, env, gitignore, pre-commit, secret-scan CI, .ship state). Future-phase docs (CLAUDE.md, PROJECT.md, ACCEPTANCE.md, …) are authored by their own phase, not scaffolded raw here.

commands.name: pack
commands.description: Build or validate a phase context pack — the minimal-sufficient context handed to a fresh phase agent (Phase-Isolated Context Pipeline).

commands.name: phase
commands.description: Run a specific ship pipeline phase (research, spec, build, qa, fix, prod, provision, deploy, monitor) for the current project.

commands.name: ship-status
commands.description: Show the ship pipeline status for the current project — the 10-phase map, the current phase and its gate, open owner sign-offs, and the prod/rollback pointer. Read-only.

commands.name: ship-update
commands.description: Reconcile a project's ship templates with the installed plugin via a real 3-way diff (baseline vs owner's file vs new template). Non-destructive — never overwrites owner content; reports conflicts to merge.

headings: Why not just ask Claude Code to build it?
